root.name: Ruy Lopez: Spanish Countergambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 d5

overview: Black meets 3.Bb5 with the counterstrike 3...d5, often followed by 4.Nxe5 dxe4 or 4.exd5 Qxd5, going for sharp open play at the cost of a pawn. White can take on e5 and develop with Nxc6 and O-O, or play for a quiet edge with 4.exd5. The Harding and Fricke gambit lines have Black giving more, with ...Qg5 hitting g2 and e5. Strong players expect White to come out ahead.

white_ideas.idea: Win the e5 pawn with Nxe5 and complete development
Trade into a pawn-up ending via Nxc6 and Qe2 or O-O
Meet ...Qg5 with accurate castling and Nxc6 ideas

black_ideas.idea: Counterattack with ...d5 and open the centre
Hit g2 and e5 with the queen and develop pieces quickly
Use the pin on e1 and the open d- and e-files

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with pawns exchanged on d5/e4
Black king still in the centre while White is a pawn up

character.notes: Open, tactical, with Black's early queen and counterattack against a king-side pawn.

gambit.notes: White can capture e5 and keep the pawn.

soundness.notes: White's extra pawn is usually kept, so Black's countergambit is dubious.

structure.notes: Central pawns come off early and lines open.

approach.notes: Seldom chosen by strong players against the Ruy Lopez.

level.notes: Dubious, so not Beginner; the tactics are quite concrete.

sublines_that_differ.name: Harding Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 d5 4. Nxe5 Qg5 5. Nxc6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black adds a queen counterattack on g2 and e5 for a second pawn.

character.reason: Open play with early queen sorties and a counterattack in the centre.

gambit.reason: Black counters with ...d5 and gives a pawn that White can keep.

soundness.reason: The pawn is usually kept by White.

structure.reason: The centre pawns trade off early.

approach.reason: Seldom chosen by strong players in the Ruy Lopez.

plans.reason: Development for a pawn with queen sorties.
